preset_rules.rich_urban: highest wealth_index among cells with population above the 80th percentile
preset_rules.poor_rural: lowest wealth_index among cells with population between the 20th and 60th percentiles and below-median road_km

steps.title: Official district GDP
steps.body: Every district has one published GDDP total, Y_g. That number is the only monetary truth in the pipeline; the model never changes it.

steps.title: Split the district into H3 cells
steps.body: The district polygon is filled with H3 resolution-7 hexagons (~5 km² each). Each hexagon becomes one node.

steps.title: Attach features to each cell
steps.body: Population (Kontur), night lights (VIIRS average_masked), OSM road km, building footprint area, landuse shares and POI counts by tag group. Magnitudes are split into an exists flag plus log10 value, then z-scored.

steps.title: Wire the graph
steps.body: Each cell links to its 6 immediate H3 neighbours, and upward to its R6 and R5 parents. Economic activity spills across hexagon borders, so a cell is described partly by its surroundings.

steps.title: Message passing
steps.body: GraphSAGE averages neighbour embeddings and mixes them with the cell's own embedding; parent cells pool their children and broadcast context back down. A GCNII initial residual keeps the original features in play at every layer.

steps.title: Node embedding
steps.body: After 4 rounds the cell holds a 64-dimensional embedding that encodes both its own features and its neighbourhood.

steps.title: Economic intensity
steps.body: A linear readout plus softplus turns the embedding into s_i ≥ 0: an unitless per-person intensity, not rupees.

steps.title: Normalised share
steps.body: Weight the intensity by population, z_i = s_i × pop_i, and sum inside the district: Z_g. The dasymetric factor is scale_g = Y_g / Z_g.

steps.title: Final cell GDP and wealth
steps.body: gdp_i = z_i × scale_g, so cells in a district sum exactly to the official Y_g. Dividing by population gives ₹/person, and its within-state percentile rank is wealth_index.

formulas: Z_g = sum_{i in district g} z_i
gdp_i = z_i * scale_g   # allocated ₹, not a measurement

training.loss: mean over districts of (log10 Σ_i s_i·pop_i − log10 Y_g)² + 0.05 · population-weighted floor hinge
training.note: The loss only ever sees district totals. Individual cell values are unidentified, which is why the range across seeds matters.

disclaimer: Cell GDP is an allocation of official district GDP, not a measurement. Ensemble range is across random seeds, not a calibrated probability of error. wealth_index is not a DHS score. NTL is in the model when the average_masked composite is present.
